newsitem.title: PANAMA: Tiomin to remain in Panama despite Indian protest.
newsitem.headline: Tiomin to remain in Panama despite Indian protest.

text.p: Officials of the local unit of Canadian mining company Tiomin Resources Inc said they plan to continue their Panamanian mining project despite protests from local Indians.

"We don't feel threatened and we don't plan to pull out. The Indians who live in the area are for the project," said Edward Kurys, director of Tiomin's project to mine the world's 12th largest copper deposit in Cerro Colorado, 220 miles (350 km) from Panama City.
Tiomin received authorization for the mine six months ago. The first set of feasibility studies should be ready next March, Kurys said.
Last week, leaders of the Ngobe-Bugle Indians, who claim the land, warned they would shut down the mining project if it was not stopped because it threatens their culture.
The Ngobe-Bugle Indians, the largest of Panama's six Indian groups with a population of 125,000, have been waiting for an Indian territory, or comarca, in the area for 25 years.
"It's incorrect that the Ngobe-Bugle will lose their culture with the project," Kurys said. "We continue to do our best to ensure the project is compatible with the culture and the comarca," he said.
